sentences.en: And during the pandemic, I started to notice something.
sentences.zh: 在大流行期间，我开始注意到一件事。

sentences.en: Customers are now paying more than ever for beef.
sentences.zh: 顾客现在为牛肉支付的费用比以往任何时候都要高。

sentences.en: Beef was getting a lot more expensive.
sentences.zh: 牛肉变得贵得多了。

sentences.en: Retail prices at record highs.
sentences.zh: 零售价创下历史新高。

sentences.en: In 2021, wholesale beef prices shot up more than 40%, and certain cuts of steak increased by more than 70%.
sentences.zh: 2021年，牛肉批发价格飙升了40%以上，某些种类的牛排涨幅超过了70%。

sentences.en: Meat lovers beware.
sentences.zh: 肉食爱好者请注意。

sentences.en: Now, the conventional wisdom was that the beef industry was just reflecting the chaos of the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 当时，传统观点认为牛肉行业只是反映了大流行的混乱。

sentences.en: Now, a major meat packaging plant has now closed because of an outbreak to employees of JBS and Greenland.
sentences.zh: 如今，由于JBS和格陵兰员工爆发疫情，一家主要的肉类包装厂已经关闭。

sentences.en: We learned that slaughterhouses shut down because of coronavirus outbreaks.
sentences.zh: 我们了解到屠宰场因冠状病毒疫情而关闭。

sentences.en: Grocers are having a hard time keeping beef and other items in stock.
sentences.zh: 杂货商很难保证牛肉和其他商品的库存。

sentences.en: There's a combination of product shortages and high demand.
sentences.zh: 这是产品短缺和高需求共同作用的结果。

sentences.en: And that was causing a shortage in supply.
sentences.zh: 这导致了供应短缺。

sentences.en: But I started to hear from sources who were telling me that there was a lot more to the price spikes.
sentences.zh: 但我开始听到消息人士告诉我，价格暴涨背后还有更多内情。

sentences.en: That this represented something larger and more fundamental.
sentences.zh: 这代表着某种更大、更根本的问题。

sentences.en: Something I'd been tracking for years.
sentences.zh: 这是我多年来一直在追踪的问题。

sentences.zh: 基本上我的一生中，我们从消费者每一块钱里分到的比例一直在下降。

sentences.en: Is that despite the expensive prices of meat that Americans were paying at the store, the profits weren't trickling down to them.
sentences.zh: 尽管美国人在商店里购买肉类的价格很昂贵，但利润并没有向下渗透到他们手中。

sentences.en: In the last couple of years, it's just gotten kind of to the point of ridiculousness.
sentences.zh: 在过去几年里，情况已经变得荒谬可笑。

sentences.en: And this, they said, was not a new phenomenon.
sentences.zh: 他们说，这并不是一个新现象。

sentences.en: A lot of people don't understand how trapped ranchers are in this really broken system.
sentences.zh: 很多人并不明白牧场主在这个真正破烂的系统中被困得有多深。

sentences.en: What was going on in the beef industry reflected decades of transformation in the American economy.
sentences.zh: 牛肉行业发生的事情反映了美国经济几十年来发生的变革。

sentences.en: Why isn't that money going to you, though?
sentences.zh: 不过，为什么这笔钱没有落到你手上？

sentences.zh: 这是一个价值百万美元的问题。

sentences.zh: 对牛肉的需求如此之高。

sentences.en: Why was it going down?
sentences.zh: 为什么它会下降？

sentences.en: There was no reason for it to go down.
sentences.zh: 它没有任何理由下降。

sentences.en: And it was bigger than beef.
sentences.zh: 而且这不仅限于牛肉。

sentences.en: I will live and die by a free market.
sentences.zh: 我生为自由市场的人，死为自由市场的鬼。

sentences.en: But if I'm not a good producer, you know, the market should be able to tell me that and say, well, you know, you can't be in business because you can't produce economically.
sentences.zh: 但如果我不是一个优秀的生产者，你知道，市场应该能告诉我这一点，并说，好吧，你知道，你不能做生意，因为你无法进行经济化生产。

sentences.en: And I will live and die by that.
sentences.zh: 我生为此死也为此。

sentences.en: But we do not have a free market.
sentences.zh: 但我们并没有一个自由市场。

sentences.en: And it doesn't give a reward to the right people.
sentences.zh: 而且它并没有给正确的人以回报。

sentences.en: This transformation was affecting all of American life.
sentences.zh: 这种变革正在影响着整个美国人的生活。

sentences.en: Supply and demand simply wasn't working the way it used to.
sentences.zh: 供求关系已经不再像过去那样运作了。

sentences.en: And in places like Colorado, Wyoming, Montana, Nebraska, Kansas, ranching becomes a dominant part of the economy.
sentences.zh: 在科罗拉多、怀俄明、蒙大拿、内布拉斯加、堪萨斯等地，牧业成为了经济的主导部分。

sentences.en: In fact, it becomes the largest part of American agriculture.
sentences.zh: 事实上，它成为了美国农业中最大的一部分。

sentences.en: So, there's money to be made here.
sentences.zh: 所以，这里有钱可赚。

sentences.en: Oh, there's a great deal of money to be made.
sentences.zh: 哦，有大量的钱可赚。

sentences.en: But remember, this is also the era of American history where the robber barons are dominant.
sentences.zh: 但请记住，这也是美国历史上强盗资本家横行的时代。

sentences.en: When Steve talks about public support for Butch Cassidy and his gang taking money from these railroad titans and bankers, that's who they're taking it from, the robber barons.
sentences.zh: 当史蒂夫谈到公众支持布奇·卡西迪和他的帮派从这些铁路大亨和银行家手中抢钱时，他们抢的就是这些人，那些强盗资本家。

sentences.en: These are the giant industrialists like John D.
sentences.zh: 这些是像约翰·D·

sentences.en: Rockefeller, Andrew Carnegie, J.P.
sentences.zh: 洛克菲勒、安德鲁·卡内基、J.P.

sentences.en: Morgan.
sentences.zh: 摩根这样的工业巨头。

sentences.en: And it's during this time that these robber barons are trying to basically establish dominant positions in all the big industries of the day.
sentences.zh: 正是在这段时间里，这些强盗资本家试图在当时的所有大行业中基本上确立主导地位。

sentences.en: Railroads, electricity, oil, finance.
sentences.zh: 铁路、电力、石油、金融。

sentences.en: And they're doing it by buying up all the smaller guys and consolidating, consolidating, consolidating.
sentences.zh: 他们通过收购所有小型竞争对手并不断进行合并、合并、再合并来做到这一点。

sentences.en: And this totally transforms the American economy.
sentences.zh: 这彻底改变了美国经济。

sentences.en: By taking control of these markets, they're able to take control of the terms of the markets, the prices, the costs.
sentences.zh: 通过控制这些市场，他们能够掌控市场的条款、价格和成本。

sentences.en: They crush labor.
sentences.zh: 他们残酷打压劳工。

sentences.en: And when they turn their attention to the cattle industry,
sentences.zh: 当他们把目光转向养牛业时，

sentences.en: what this looks like is they go around buying up all the local slaughterhouses and turning them into these giant slaughterhouse conglomerates.
sentences.zh: 情况就是他们四处收购当地的屠宰场，并将其变成这些庞大的屠宰场企业集团。

sentences.en: So that by 1917, there are just five dominant so-called meat packers in the whole country.
sentences.zh: 因此，到1917年，全国只剩下五家占主导地位的所谓肉类加工商。

sentences.en: These are the companies that slaughter cattle and distribute them.
sentences.zh: 这些公司负责屠宰肉牛并进行分销。

sentences.en: And the result is just horrifying conditions inside these packing plants, not only for the animals, but also for the people working inside the plants.
sentences.zh: 结果是这些加工厂内部的条件极其骇人，不仅对动物如此，对在厂里工作的工人也是如此。

sentences.en: The public comes to learn about unbelievably crowded meat packing plants that reek of rotting flesh, trash, innards lying around, attracting rodents.
sentences.zh: 公众开始了解到拥挤不堪的肉类加工厂，那里散发着腐烂血肉、垃圾和内脏的恶臭，吸引着啮齿动物。

sentences.en: And along with this growing understanding of these terrible working conditions comes this broader awareness of the robber barons and how they're growing richer and richer.
sentences.zh: 随着对这些糟糕工作环境的深入了解，人们也更广泛地认识到强盗资本家如何变得越来越富有。

sentences.en: They're monopolizing the bounty of American capitalism.
sentences.zh: 他们垄断了美国资本主义的红利。

sentences.en: And their wealth is really coming at the expense of everyone else.
sentences.zh: 他们的财富实际上是建立在牺牲其他所有人的基础之上的。

sentences.en: Eventually, there's outrage against these industrialists.
sentences.zh: 最终，公众对这些实业家感到愤怒。

sentences.en: It comes to a head and we get a wave of regulation.
sentences.zh: 矛盾激化，我们迎来了监管浪潮。

sentences.en: And in the cattle industry, we get the Packers and Stockyards Act of 1921.
sentences.zh: 在养牛业，我们迎来了1921年的《包装商和饲养场法案》。

sentences.en: And it's aimed directly at the meat packers.
sentences.zh: 该法案直接针对肉类加工商。

sentences.en: It bars them from price manipulation.
sentences.zh: 它禁止他们操纵价格。

sentences.en: It bans the big packers from giving preferential deals to ranchers that they're aligned with and from discriminating against others.
sentences.zh: 它禁止大型加工商向与其结盟的牧场主提供优惠交易，并禁止歧视其他人。

sentences.en: This is truly a landmark piece of legislation that levels the playing field in the beef industry.
sentences.zh: 这确实是一项具有里程碑意义的立法，平息了牛肉行业的竞争环境。

sentences.en: I'm happy to report that after years of uncertainty, culminating in the collapse of the spring of 1933,
sentences.zh: 我很高兴地向大家报告，经过多年的不确定性并在1933年春季的崩溃达到顶峰之后，

sentences.en: we are bringing order out of the old chaos with a greater certainty of the employment of labor at a reasonable wage and of more business at a fair profit.
sentences.zh: 我们正在从旧的混乱中恢复秩序，使劳动力的合理工资就业和以合理利润开展更多业务变得更加确定。

sentences.en: And ultimately, this era of government cracking down on the excessive power of big business, combined really with the trauma of the Great Depression, delivers FDR's New Deal,
sentences.zh: 最终，政府打击大企业过度权力的这一时代，再加上大萧条的创伤，带来了罗斯福的新政，

sentences.en: a monumental change to American life.
sentences.zh: 这是对美国生活具有划时代意义的改变。

sentences.en: Which rests upon us all, we have the right to expect that this driving power will be given patriotically and wholeheartedly to our nation.
sentences.zh: 这一切落在我们每个人肩上，我们有权期望这种驱动力能够爱国且全心全意地奉献给我们的国家。

sentences.en: This is really the new economic landscape that Steve's dad enters when he decides to follow in his father's footsteps 30 years later, as he arrives in Montana in 1950.
sentences.zh: 这确实是史蒂夫的父亲在30年后的1950年抵达蒙大拿州、决定子承父业时所面对的新经济格局。

sentences.en: Ranches were dirt cheap at that time here.
sentences.zh: 那时候这里的牧场便宜得要命。

sentences.en: It was like they bought their first ranch for like $3 an acre.
sentences.zh: 就像他们买第一个牧场时，每英亩只要3美元左右。

sentences.en: This is where Steve is born, where he grows up with his three siblings.
sentences.zh: 这就是史蒂夫出生的地方，也是他和三个兄弟姐妹一起长大的地方。

sentences.en: They're all engaged in the day-in, day-out operation of tending to the herd.
sentences.zh: 他们都参与了照料牛群的日常运营。

sentences.en: You said in the third grade you were driving machinery around?
sentences.zh: 你说你在三年级的时候就在开机器了？

sentences.en: That's also when I've started like driving the pickups and things.
sentences.zh: 那也是我开始学着开皮卡之类的时候。

sentences.en: Nine years old, you're driving a pickup.
sentences.zh: 九岁，你就在开皮卡了。

sentences.en: Is it on the property or not on the highway to it?
sentences.zh: 是在私有土地上还是在去公路的路上？

sentences.en: On the property, yeah.
sentences.zh: 在私有土地上，对。

sentences.en: Well, sometimes on the county roads.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有时也在乡间小路上。

sentences.en: But, you know, when you push the clutch in, you'd have to go down so, like, you lose all visibility for a while, shift,
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，当你踩下离合器时，你得踩得很深，以至于有一会儿你会完全看不到前面，然后换挡，

sentences.en: and then kind of come up where you can see above the dashboard.
sentences.zh: 接着再探出头来，好让视线能越过仪表盘。

sentences.en: And I don't know, we just, nobody thought anything of it, you know what I mean?
sentences.zh: 我不知道，我们就是觉得这没什么，你知道我的意思吗？

sentences.en: But every year, the big moment they're building toward comes when they load up their cattle into stock cars and drives them the couple of hours to Billings, to the auction house.
sentences.zh: 但每年让他们翘首以盼的大时刻，就是把牛装进牲口棚车，花上几个小时开到比利斯的拍卖行。

sentences.en: You're always kind of like, oh, God, I hope, you know, we don't have a blowout, because, you know, you're doing it on old tires.
sentences.zh: 你总是会想，哦，天哪，我希望，你知道的，我们可别爆胎，因为你知道，你用的是旧轮胎。

sentences.en: The auction house was this place where you'd have sellers, like Steve's dad, coming from all over with their cows, from clear across Montana, from as far away as the Dakotas.
sentences.zh: 拍卖行是个汇聚各地卖牛人的地方，比如史蒂夫的父亲，他们带着牛从蒙大拿州的四面八方赶来，甚至远至达科他州。

sentences.en: And then you'd have buyers coming, in some cases, from even further away, from Nebraska, from Colorado, all looking to buy cows.
sentences.zh: 然后你会看到买家前来，在某些情况下，他们来自更远的地方，比如内布拉斯加州、科罗拉多州，所有人都是来买牛的。

sentences.en: This big, bustling, noisy cow market.
sentences.zh: 这是一个巨大、喧闹、熙熙攘攘的牛市。

sentences.en: You know, when we would come to town, that was the social, that's where you'd go and see your neighbors and friends.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，当我们来到镇上时，那就是社交活动，那是你去见邻居和朋友的地方。

sentences.en: And so, that was always a big part of my life, was like, you know, it was always kind of a cool place to go.
sentences.zh: 所以，那一直是我生活中的很大一部分，你知道的，那总是一个挺酷的去处。

sentences.en: It's important to understand that the decision to take their animals to the auction, that was about the most important decision they could make in the course of the year.
sentences.zh: 必须要明白，决定把牲畜送到拍卖行，可以说是他们一年当中做出的最重要的决定。

sentences.en: It really determined their income for the year.
sentences.zh: 这 realmente 决定了他们那一年的收入。

sentences.en: If they thought the market was going to get better, you know, and they're, you know, they're looking at the commodities prices on the Chicago Board of Trade.
sentences.zh: 如果他们认为市场会好转，你知道的，他们会查看芝加哥商品交易所的大宗商品价格。

sentences.en: They're talking to their neighbors to see what they're receiving for their animals.
sentences.zh: 他们会和邻居交谈，看看他们的动物能卖多少钱。

sentences.en: If they think they're going to make more later, then they keep feeding their calves.
sentences.zh: 如果他们认为以后能赚更多，那他们就会继续喂养小牛。

sentences.en: They let them run around on the pasture, and they accept the increased costs of caring for them, assuming that they'll capture a better price down the road.
sentences.zh: 让他们在牧场上奔跑，并接受照顾他们不断增加的成本，指望以后能卖个好价钱。

sentences.en: And if they think the market's going to worsen, then they're more likely to load the animals, take them to the auction, and get rid of them.
sentences.zh: 如果他们认为市场会恶化，那么他们更有可能把牲畜装车，带到拍卖行卖掉。

sentences.en: What was that like?
sentences.zh: 那是什么样的体验？

sentences.en: Could you get a fair price?
sentences.zh: 你能得到一个公平的价格吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, it was more competitive then.
sentences.zh: 对，我是说，那时候竞争更激烈。

sentences.en: And they have some confidence in those years that the auction house is a real market.
sentences.zh: 而且他们在那些年里对拍卖行是一个真正的市场充满信心。

sentences.en: You know, there are representatives from the packers.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，那里有加工商的代表。

sentences.en: There are buyers for feedlots.
sentences.zh: 有饲养场的买家。

sentences.en: Feedlots, there are large numbers of people crowding the stalls, looking at the animals being let in on display.
sentences.zh: 饲养场，有大量的人挤在围栏边，看着被放出来展示的动物。

sentences.en: They'll have good calves now.
sentences.zh: 他们现在会有很好的小牛。

sentences.en: Yes, sir.
sentences.zh: 是的，先生。

sentences.en: Solid mouth cows all night here.
sentences.zh: 今晚这都是牙口好的壮牛。

sentences.en: And there's kind of a frenzy of buying when there's demand.
sentences.zh: 当有需求时，买卖会变得非常狂热。

sentences.en: So ranchers like Steve's dad have some assurance that once they bring their animals to the marketplace, there's truly a market that will give them a fair price for their animals.
sentences.zh: 所以像史蒂夫父亲这样的牧场主有一定程度的保证，一旦他们把动物带到市场上，这里确实有一个市场会为他们的动物给出公平的价格。

sentences.en: Right, because the era of consolidation is over.
sentences.zh: 没错，因为企业兼并的时代已经结束了。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没，错。

sentences.en: The era of consolidation is over, and there are now lots of slaughterhouses.
sentences.zh: 兼并时代已经结束，现在有很多屠宰场。

sentences.en: There are medium-sized companies, there are larger companies, but there are all sorts of channels that the charters can use to sell their animals.
sentences.zh: 有中型公司，也有大型公司，但牧场主可以通过各种渠道来销售他们的动物。

sentences.en: So typically, the day ends happily.
sentences.zh: 所以通常情况下，一天会在快乐中结束。

sentences.en: You've got that check, you can pay your bills, you can pay the bank back.
sentences.zh: 你拿到了支票，你可以付清账单，你可以还清银行的贷款。

sentences.en: And his dad drives home satisfied with a check in hand that's big enough to cover his costs, to pay for the debt on his land,
sentences.zh: 他的父亲带着一张足以支付成本、偿还土地债务的支票心满意足地开车回家，

sentences.en: and to continue at a real middle-class standard for another year.
sentences.zh: 并能以真正的中产阶级标准再过一年。

sentences.en: But as Steve grew up, he wasn't sure that this was the life for him.
sentences.zh: 但随着史蒂夫长大，他并不确定这是否是他想要的生活。

sentences.en: I didn't really have any intentions of being a rancher.
sentences.zh: 我其实压根没打算当个牧场主。

sentences.en: Until he met a woman named Jeannie from Chicago.
sentences.zh: 直到他遇到了一位来自芝加哥名叫珍妮的女性。

sentences.en: Part of the reason I think she wanted to get married is she was just totally attracted to this life.
sentences.zh: 我想她想结婚的部分原因，是她完全被这种生活所吸引。

sentences.en: You know, she loved animals, she loved the horses, she loved the business, she loved the country.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，她喜欢动物，喜欢马，喜欢这里的生意，喜欢这片土地。

sentences.en: That was the end of any thoughts of Steve giving up ranching.
sentences.zh: 史蒂夫放弃养牛的想法到此为止。

sentences.en: But actually, it was Steve's father who counseled him to get out and do something else.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，正是史蒂夫的父亲劝告他离开这里去干别的。

sentences.en: He did everything he possibly could to discourage me and everybody else to going into ranching, because he saw all this coming.
sentences.zh: 他竭尽所能地劝阻我和其他人不要从事养牛业，因为他预见到了这一切的发生。

sentences.en: He saw it all coming.
sentences.zh: 他预见了这一切。

sentences.en: Like, what did he see?
sentences.zh: 比如，他看到了什么？

sentences.en: That these family farms and ranches wouldn't be viable, you know.
sentences.zh: 他看到这些家庭农场和牧场将难以为继，你知道的。

sentences.en: My dad kind of convinced me that it probably wasn't the best thing to be doing, but on the other hand, I couldn't really imagine doing anything else.
sentences.zh: 我爸爸算是说服了我，觉得这可能不是最好的选择，但另一方面，我真的想象不出自己还能做什么。

sentences.en: So Steve hears his dad's warnings, but he decides to keep going.
sentences.zh: 所以史蒂夫听到了父亲的警告，但他决定继续坚持下去。

sentences.en: And when Steve's dad dies in 1979, Steve ends up taking over the ranch.
sentences.zh: 当史蒂夫的父亲于1979年去世时，史蒂夫最终接管了牧场。

sentences.en: Thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: That same year, a man named Ronald Reagan announces that he's running for president of the United States.
sentences.zh: 就在那一年，一个叫罗纳德·里根的人宣布竞选美国总统。

sentences.en: I've lived in an America where those who often had too little to eat outnumbered those who had enough.
sentences.zh: 我经历过这样一个美国：那些常常食不果腹的人比那些衣食无忧的人还要多。

sentences.en: And I've seen our country face financial ruin in the Depression.
sentences.zh: 我曾目睹我们的国家在大萧条中面临经济崩溃。

sentences.en: As president, I would use every power at my command to make the federal establishment respond to the will and the collective wishes of the people.
sentences.zh: 作为总统，我将动用我手中的每一项权力，让联邦体制去回应人民的意志和共同愿望。

sentences.en: We must force the entire federal bureaucracy to live in the real world of reduced spending, streamlined function, and accountability to the people it serves.
sentences.zh: 我们必须强迫整个联邦官僚机构生活在现实世界中，削减开支，简化职能，并对它所服务的人民负责。

sentences.en: And that sets in motion a series of events that once again transforms the American economy and eventually turns Steve's dad's fears into reality.
sentences.zh: 这就引发了一系列事件，再次改变了美国经济，并最终将史蒂夫父亲的担忧变成了现实。

sentences.en: Thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 已解锁？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但是，如果你能免费试用《时报》一个月，且无需绑定信用卡，会怎么样？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在应用中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 给你一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能看到什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用，即可免费体验30天。

sentences.en: And I don't believe the American people are frightened by what lies ahead.
sentences.zh: 我不相信美国人民会被前方未知的道路所吓倒。

sentences.en: Together, we're going to do what has to be done.
sentences.zh: 齐心协力，我们将完成必须要做的事。

sentences.en: We're going to put America back to work again.
sentences.zh: 我们要让美国重新工作起来。

sentences.en: So, Peter, what role does the Reagan administration play in this story?
sentences.zh: 那么，彼得，里根政府在这个故事中扮演了什么角色？

sentences.en: Well, Reagan ushers in a period of extraordinary deregulation.
sentences.zh: 嗯，里根开启了一个非同寻常的放松监管的时期。

sentences.en: He really represents the bookend to the New Deal.
sentences.zh: 他确实代表了新政的终结篇。

sentences.en: Overregulation causes small and independent businessmen and women, as well as large businesses, to defer or terminate plans for expansion.
sentences.zh: 过度监管导致中小型企业主以及大企业推迟或终止了扩张计划。

sentences.en: We have inflation in great measure because the federal government has lived too well.
sentences.zh: 我们遭遇严重通货膨胀很大程度上是因为联邦政府的日子过得太优渥了。

sentences.en: And by that, I mean it has become bloated.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它变得臃肿不堪。

sentences.en: Now, we have no intention of dismantling the regulatory agencies.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们无意解散监管机构。

sentences.en: However, we must come to grips with inefficient and burdensome regulations.
sentences.zh: 然而，我们必须着手解决那些低效且沉重的监管规定。

sentences.en: Eliminate those we can and reform the others.
sentences.zh: 废除我们能废除的，改革其余的。

sentences.en: Our aim is to increase our national wealth so all will have more.
sentences.zh: 我们的目标是增加国家财富，让所有人都能拥有更多。

sentences.en: Not just redistribute what we already have, which is just a sharing of scarcity.
sentences.zh: 而不是仅仅重新分配我们已有的东西，那只是在分享贫穷。

sentences.en: If we view the New Deal as a reaction to excessive monopoly power by the robber barons, Reagan represents a whole new view of government in which government,
sentences.zh: 如果我们把新政视为对强盗大亨过度垄断权力的反弹，里根则代表了一种全新的政府观，即政府——

sentences.en: as he famously puts it, people keep looking to government for the answer and government's the problem, is not the solution, but the problem itself.
sentences.zh: 正如他那句名言所说，人们总是指望政府来解决问题，而政府就是问题所在，它不是解药，而是问题本身。

sentences.en: He embraces the thinking of Milton Friedman, the economist who's considered the sort of godfather of neoliberalism,
sentences.zh: 他拥抱了米尔顿·弗里德曼的思想，这位经济学家被视为新自由主义的某种教父，

sentences.en: who represents the idea that a market left to its own devices is the best way to maximize wealth for everyone.
sentences.zh: 他代表这样一种观点：任由市场自行发展，是为所有人实现财富最大化的最佳途径。

sentences.en: The essence of a capitalist system in its pure form is that it is a system of cooperation without compulsion, of voluntary exchange, of free enterprise.
sentences.zh: 纯粹形式的资本主义体系的本质，在于它是一个没有强制的合作体系、自由交换体系和自由企业体系。

sentences.en: And who actually specifically calls the robber baron era...
sentences.zh: 而且是谁具体将强盗大亨时代称之为……

sentences.en: The robber baron myth.
sentences.zh: 强盗大亨的神话。

sentences.en: A myth.
sentences.zh: 一个神话。

sentences.en: The myth that it was a period in which particularly the farmers of the Middle West were being ground beneath the rapacious activities of the Wall Street financiers.
sentences.zh: 那种认为在中西部地区的农民受到华尔街金融家贪婪行径残酷剥削的时期，其实是一个神话。

sentences.en: Reagan also embraces the thinking of another important academic, Robert Bork, who plays a crucial role in changing the American understanding of antitrust law.
sentences.zh: 里根还接受了另一位重要学者罗伯特·博克的思想，他在改变美国对反垄断法的理解方面发挥了关键作用。

sentences.en: My entire book is premised on the question of what best serves consumers.
sentences.zh: 我整本书的出发点都是什么能最好地服务消费者。

sentences.en: But everything in that book is an argument from consumer welfare.
sentences.zh: 但那本书里的所有内容，都是基于消费者福利的论证。

sentences.en: So previously, monopolies were simply seen as bad for everyone.
sentences.zh: 所以在过去，垄断被简单地视为对所有人都有害。

sentences.en: Well, Bork argues and becomes mainstream in this view that so long as consumer prices are unchanged or dropping, then we should actually welcome scale.
sentences.zh: 而博克则认为——这种观点后来成为主流——只要消费者的价格没有上涨或在下降，我们其实就应该欢迎规模化。

sentences.en: Reagan embraces all of this.
sentences.zh: 里根全盘接受了这一切。

sentences.en: And his administration makes clear things are going to be different now.
sentences.zh: 他的政府明确表示，现在一切都要变了。

sentences.en: And a whole new set of principles are operative.
sentences.zh: 一套全新的原则正在发挥作用。

sentences.en: It's time to try something different.
sentences.zh: 是时候尝试一些不同的东西了。

sentences.en: And that's what we're going to do.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们要做的。

sentences.en: And Peter, what does this all actually look like as we start to see these new principles become policy in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 皮特，当这些新原则开始在美国变成政策时，

sentences.en: under Reagan?
sentences.zh: 在里根执政期间，这一切到底是什么样的？

sentences.en: Basically, what happens is, and we're talking about across every industry, the Reagan administration stops enforcing antitruSt.
sentences.zh: 基本上发生的情况是——我们说的是各个行业——里根政府停止执行反垄断法。

sentences.en: They don't challenge mergers.
sentences.zh: 他们不再对兼并提出异议。

sentences.en: This allows big companies, just like in the early 1900s, to once again go on buying sprees, including the meatpackers.
sentences.zh: 这使得大公司得以像20世纪初那样，再次开始疯狂收购，包括肉类加工商。

sentences.en: When was the first clear sign that, you know, uh-oh, the economics of this thing have changed, and maybe my dad was right,
sentences.zh: 什么时候你才第一次清晰地感觉到，呃噢，这里的经济学已经变了，也许我爸爸是对的，

sentences.en: and this is where we're headed, to a place where it's not viable to make a living doing this?
sentences.zh: 而我们正走向这样一个地方：靠这个谋生已经行不通了？

sentences.en: That was in the mid-80s.
sentences.zh: 那是在80年代中期。

sentences.en: That's when, you know, the Packers started consolidating.
sentences.zh: 也就是那时，肉类加工商开始进行整合。

sentences.en: And then at the same time, we were also aware of what was happening in the chicken and hog industries.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，我们也注意到了鸡肉和生猪行业正在发生的变化。

sentences.en: The Packers promise that through this consolidation, through engaging in these large deals, they're going to revolutionize the food industry.
sentences.zh: 加工商承诺，通过这种整合，通过参与这些大交易，他们将彻底革新食品行业。

sentences.en: They're going to lower beef prices for American consumers through economies of scale, which will allow them to cut costs.
sentences.zh: 他们将通过规模效应降低美国消费者的牛肉价格，从而使他们能够削减成本。

sentences.en: They concentrate slaughterhouses in fewer and fewer hands.
sentences.zh: 他们将屠宰场集中在越来越少的人手中。

sentences.en: And just like we saw in the last century, they start closing down competitors.
sentences.zh: 正如我们在上个世纪所看到的，他们开始关闭竞争对手。

sentences.en: The result is that, once again, ranchers like the Charters are left with fewer options for where they can sell their cattle, and they're getting less for their animals.
sentences.zh: 结果是，像查特夫妇这样的牧场主再次发现，他们出售牛只的选择变少了，他们从动物身上赚到的钱也变少了。

sentences.en: So, what this means for Steve and his ranch is that by the late 1980s, more years than not, he's barely breaking even.
sentences.zh: 因此，对史蒂夫和他的牧场来说，这意味着到了20世纪80年代末，大部分年份他都只能勉强维持收支平衡。

sentences.en: So, you know, when the prices started getting, you know, where I knew it wouldn't cover the cost, then we decided, well, there's got to be a different way.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，当价格开始变得——你知道的——让我知道它无法弥补成本时，我们就决定，肯定有别的出路。

sentences.en: So, we started exploring different ways.
sentences.zh: 于是，我们开始探索不同的方法。

sentences.en: He turns to this slaughterhouse that he used to do business with.
sentences.zh: 他找回了这家他以前曾有过业务往来的屠宰场。

sentences.en: It initially probably went out of business in probably the early 70s, and then I was actually involved with some ranchers that tried to get it going again back in.
sentences.zh: 它可能在大约70年代初倒闭了，后来我实际上参与了一些牧场主的活动，试图在某个时候让它重新开业。

sentences.en: And they do this because they're hoping to inject more competition in the marketplace.
sentences.zh: 他们这样做是希望向市场注入更多竞争。

sentences.en: Instead of simply having to sell to the packers, who are operating fewer and fewer slaughterhouses, they'll have a local option where they can slaughter their animals.
sentences.zh: 他们不必只能卖给那些屠宰场越来越少的加工商，而是有了一个当地的选择来屠宰他们的动物。

sentences.en: So, the way I've heard the story locally is the packers get wind of this project, and they set about to sabotage it by briefly paying a premium to local ranchers
sentences.zh: 所以，我从当地听到的故事是，加工商风闻了这个项目，他们开始通过短暂地向当地牧场主支付溢价来破坏它，

sentences.en: to deprive the Billings Slaughterhouse of the volume that it needs to break even.
sentences.zh: 以此剥夺比灵斯屠宰场实现收支平衡所需的业务量。

sentences.en: Long story short, in less than a year, that plant closes again, and the charters are out $100,000.
sentences.zh: 长话短说，在不到一年的时间里，那家工厂再次关闭，查特夫妇损失了10万美元。

sentences.en: It was kind of a disaster, and we lost a lot of money.
sentences.zh: 这简直是一场灾难，我们损失了巨额资金。

sentences.en: It was a very unpleasant prospect.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常令人不愉快的局面。

sentences.en: So, Jeannie then has another idea.
sentences.zh: 于是珍妮想出了另一个主意。

sentences.en: This is Steve's wife.
sentences.zh: 这是史蒂夫的妻子。

sentences.en: Why don't we just try to circumvent the packers altogether?
sentences.zh: 我们为什么不直接绕过加工商呢？

sentences.en: Instead of dealing with the middleman, let's sell our beef directly to the people who are distributing it to customers.
sentences.zh: 与其跟中间商打交道，不如直接把我们的牛肉卖给向客户分销牛肉的人。

sentences.en: That's supermarkets.
sentences.zh: 也就是超级市场。

sentences.en: And so, Jeannie had got to know this.
sentences.zh: 所以，珍妮当时了解到了这一点。

sentences.en: There was a grocery store in Billings called the County Market,
sentences.zh: 比灵斯有一家杂货店叫乡村市场，

sentences.en: and he had been very cooperative in doing these beef promotion kind of things.
sentences.zh: 店主在搞这种牛肉促销活动时非常配合。

sentences.en: So, she went to him and said, you know, we could probably get these slaughtered locally, and would you sell our beef?
sentences.zh: 于是她去找他说，你知道，我们或许可以在当地屠宰这些牛肉，你愿意卖我们的牛肉吗？

sentences.en: He was receptive to that.
sentences.zh: 他对这个提议很接受。

sentences.en: So, we went up, set up in the parking lot.
sentences.zh: 于是我们开车过去，在停车场摆了摊。

sentences.en: The first weekend, they drive down to Billings.
sentences.zh: 第一个周末，他们开车来到比灵斯。

sentences.en: They grilled samples of their beef, and it was hugely popular.
sentences.zh: 他们在现场烤了牛肉样品，大受欢迎。

sentences.en: People were like, wow, this is great.
sentences.zh: 人们纷纷表示，哇，这太棒了。

sentences.en: So, we were there having a great time selling beef.
sentences.zh: 所以我们当时卖牛肉卖得很开心。

sentences.en: People were coming in with grocery carts, filling it up to take it home and freeze it.
sentences.zh: 人们推着购物车进来，装满牛肉带回家冻起来。

sentences.en: You know, it's like it was, you know, and we were going, yeah, this is going to work.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当时的感觉就是，我们觉得，这下行得通了。

sentences.en: But then?
sentences.zh: 但接下来呢？

sentences.en: Went by the meat manager who we talked to, and he said, oh, that's funny.
sentences.zh: 我们聊过的那个肉类经理想起这事，他说，哦，真有意思。

sentences.en: The buyer from IBP, which was one of the big ones at the time, Iowa Beef Packers, he said, oh, I hadn't seen him in a long time, you know.
sentences.zh: IBP（当时的大企业之一，爱荷华牛肉加工商）的采购员说，哦，我好久没见到他了。

sentences.en: The manager at the store tells them that the Packers paid a visit and told them that this was no-go.
sentences.zh: 店经理告诉他们，加工商来过这里，并告诉他们此路不通。

sentences.en: They had to stop buying beef from the charters.
sentences.zh: 他们必须停止向查特夫妇购买牛肉。

sentences.en: He said, we can't sell your beef anymore.
sentences.zh: 他说，我们不能再卖你们的牛肉了。

sentences.en: If we buy your beef, they're not going to supply us, and that's our main supplier.
sentences.zh: 如果我们买你们的牛肉，他们就不给我们供货了，而他们是我们的主要供应商。

sentences.en: And Jeannie was going to, she wanted to keep, go on.
sentences.zh: 珍妮当时还想继续坚持下去。

sentences.en: And I said, God, you know, I'm not going to lose the ranch over this.
sentences.zh: 而我说，天哪，你知道的，我可不想为此把牧场搭进去。

sentences.en: So, I basically kind of chickened out, and she kind of went along.
sentences.zh: 所以我基本上算是临阵退缩了，她也只好作罢。

sentences.en: But it kind of took the heart out of me as far as fighting these things.
sentences.zh: 但就与这些势力抗争而言，这也彻底击垮了我的心气。

sentences.en: So, that marks the end of the charters' efforts to find a way to work around the Packers.
sentences.zh: 这就标志着查特夫妇寻找绕过加工商方法的努力宣告结束。

sentences.en: And they resign themselves to selling their cattle inside this system where they know that year after year, if everything goes right, they'll be fortunate to simply break even.
sentences.zh: 他们只能逆来顺受，在这个系统内继续卖牛——他们深知，年复一年，哪怕一切顺利，能勉强保本就已经算走运了。

sentences.en: But Peter, this whole approach to government and deregulation, as you said, is about the consumer.
sentences.zh: 但皮特，正如你所说，这种政府和放松管制的整体方法，一切都是为了消费者。

sentences.en: So, as the charters see less and less money for their meat, that is translating to cheaper beef prices for American consumers, right?
sentences.zh: 那么，当查特夫妇从他们的肉类中获得的收入越来越少时，这就会转化为美国消费者更便宜的牛肉价格，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, for a while.
sentences.zh: 是的，有一阵子是这样的。

sentences.en: But this idea that Bork advances, that so long as consumer prices don't go up immediately after a merger, well, then we shouldn't be troubled, this just doesn't pan out.
sentences.zh: 但博克提出的这种观点——只要消费者的价格在兼并后没有立即上涨，我们就无需担忧——根本站不住脚。

sentences.en: Now, what consolidation really does is it gives these massive companies, like the meat packers, control of the supply chain.
sentences.zh: 现在，兼并真正带来的结果是，它让这些像肉类加工商这样的巨头掌控了供应链。

sentences.en: They can control not only the relationships with the ranchers, but also the other end of the equation.
sentences.zh: 他们不仅可以控制与牧场主的关系，还可以控制等式的另一端。

sentences.en: They can dictate the prices that they're going to charge grocery stores, supermarket chains, and restaurants.
sentences.zh: 他们可以主导向杂货店、连锁超市和餐馆收取的定价。

sentences.en: And the result of this is that they're ending up with better profit margins while everyone else ends up with less.
sentences.zh: 其结果是，他们获得了更高的利润率，而其他所有人分到的却越来越少。

sentences.en: This is the story, not just of cattle ranchers and meat packers, but really of the American economy writ large going back to the 1980s.
sentences.zh: 这不仅是养牛场主和肉类加工商的故事，实际上也是追溯到20世纪80年代的整个美国经济的缩影。

sentences.en: Well, let's talk about why that continues to be the case.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们来谈谈为什么这种情况会一直持续下去。

sentences.en: Obviously, at some point, the Reagan administration ends.
sentences.zh: 显然，里根政府总有结束的时候。

sentences.en: So what happens once that era is over?
sentences.zh: 那么那个时代结束后会发生什么？

sentences.en: Well, Reagan represents the beginning of the story, but it's really just the beginning because what we've seen happen since,
sentences.zh: 嗯，里根代表了这个故事的开端，但这真的只是一个开始，因为此后我们看到的情况是——

sentences.en: I mean, really, in every administration that follows is an unwillingness to challenge this idea that the bottom line matters above all else.
sentences.zh: 我是说，实际上在随后的每一届政府中，都有一种不愿挑战以下这种观念的倾向：即利润永远高于一切。

sentences.en: And that goes for Republicans and Democrats.
sentences.zh: 无论是共和党人还是民主党人都是如此。

sentences.en: I mean, you might be tempted to think that liberal Democrats would be the natural opponents of monopoly power, but there's this interesting dynamic that we see time and again
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你可能会倾向于认为自由派民主党人会是垄断权力的天然反对者，但我们一次又一次地看到这样一种有趣的动态：

sentences.en: where that view bumps into the promise of low costs for poorer Americans.
sentences.zh: 这种观点与为贫困美国人降低成本的承诺发生了冲突。

sentences.en: And we see Democrats repeatedly siding with producers promising to deliver food at lower prices through greater scale.
sentences.zh: 我们看到民主党人一再站在那些承诺通过扩大规模来以更低价格提供食品的生产商一边。

sentences.en: Our administration is working hard to give the American people a government that works better and costs less.
sentences.zh: 我们的行政部门正在努力为美国人民提供一个办事更高效、成本更低廉的政府。

sentences.en: Thanks to the work of Vice President Gore, we are eliminating 16,000 pages of unnecessary rules
sentences.zh: 多亏了副总统戈尔的工作，我们正在废除1.6万页不必要的规章

sentences.en: and regulations, shifting more decision making out of Washington, back to states and local communities.
sentences.zh: 和条例，将更多的决策权从华盛顿下放回各州和地方社区。

sentences.en: You see this with Bill Clinton, who especially embraces the idea that consolidation is positive for Americans.
sentences.zh: 你在比尔·克林顿身上就能看到这一点，他尤其拥护企业整合对美国人有利这一观点。

sentences.en: And when it comes to beef, positive for the food supply and for programs that depend on cheap food, like food stamps.
sentences.zh: 当涉及到牛肉时，这对食品供应以及依赖廉价食品的项目（如食品券）都是有利的。

sentences.en: So he and other liberals look away from their maybe natural aversion to monopoly power, and they embrace this idea that's sold to them by the Packers, that the best way to defeat
sentences.zh: 因此，他和其它自由派不再执着于他们对垄断权力的天然反感，而是接受了加工商向他们兜售的理念：战胜贫困的最佳方式，

sentences.en: poverty is to allow the producers of food to do what they do really well, and that's figure out how to produce more food cheaply.
sentences.zh: 是让食品生产者做他们最擅长的事，也就是想方设法以低成本生产更多食品。

sentences.en: So in this quid pro quo, Democrats also support consolidation and support the interests of big corporations like the meatpackers, because in theory, it's good for poor Americans.
sentences.zh: 因此，在这场利益交换中，民主党人也支持行业整合，支持像肉类加工商这样的大企业的利益，因为从理论上讲，这对贫困的美国人是有利的。

sentences.en: Well, that's the story that everybody buys into, lubricated by campaign donations, by lobbying,
sentences.zh: 嗯，这就是在政治捐款和游说润色下，每个人都笃信的故事：

sentences.en: that the war on poverty requires low-cost food, and the way you get low-cost food is by large,
sentences.zh: 反贫困战争需要低成本食品，而获得低成本食品的途径，就是允许大型、

sentences.en: efficient companies that are allowed to amass scale, continuing to consolidate the marketplace.
sentences.zh: 高效的公司不断扩大规模，并继续在市场上进行整合。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And thus, we arrive at a bipartisan consensus that it's okay for the packing industry, and really every industry, to get smaller and smaller and more and more consolidated.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们达成了这样一种两党共识：包装行业，以及实际上每一个行业，变得越来越小、整合度越来越高，是完全可以接受的。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, by the early 2000s, the beef industry enters its biggest wave of consolidation.
sentences.zh: 因此，到20世纪2000年代初，牛肉行业迎来了其最大的一波整合浪潮。

sentences.en: Major acquisitions in the processing industry top this week's cattle industry news.
sentences.zh: 加工行业的重大收购占据了本周养牛业新闻的头条。

sentences.en: We see the industry increasingly concentrated.
sentences.zh: 我们看到行业的集中度越来越高。

sentences.en: Sanderson Farms is being acquired for $4.5 billion.
sentences.zh: 桑德森农场正以45亿美元的价格被收购。

sentences.en: Year after year.
sentences.zh: 年复一年。

sentences.en: JBS, the Brazilian company that acquired Swift & Company last year, has announced the purchase of Smithfield Beef Group and National Beef.
sentences.zh: 去年收购了斯威夫特公司的巴西企业JBS宣布，将收购史密斯菲尔德牛肉集团和全国牛肉公司。

sentences.en: We see large players swallow up smaller players.
sentences.zh: 我们看到大玩家吞并小玩家。

sentences.en: Tyson Foods officially announced it has reached a definitive agreement to buy the Keystone Foods business from Marfrey Global Foods for $2.16 billion in cash.
sentences.zh: 泰森食品正式宣布已达成最终协议，以21.6亿美元现金从马弗雷全球食品公司收购基斯通食品业务。

sentences.en: We see the smallest players disappear, unable to compete.
sentences.zh: 我们看到由于无力竞争，最小的玩家消失了。

sentences.en: The company's plan to combine Sanderson Farms with Wayne Farms, a continental grain subsidiary, to form a new privately held business.
sentences.zh: 该公司计划将桑德森农场与大陆谷物旗下的韦恩农场合并，组成一个新的私营企业。

sentences.en: The Smithfield acquisition also includes Five Rivers Cattle Feeding, the nation's largest cattle feeder.
sentences.zh: 对史密斯菲尔德的收购还包括全美最大的育牛企业——五河育牛公司。

sentences.en: We see the biggest players of all expand their reach so that they're ultimately as large or bigger than they were in the previous century.
sentences.zh: 我们看到最大的巨头进一步扩大势力范围，最终规模达到甚至超过了上个世纪的水平。

sentences.en: But these latest announcements are likely to raise more concerns about competition in the
sentences.zh: 但这些最新公告可能会引发人们对该行业竞争状况的更多担忧，

sentences.en: industry because they would essentially consolidate the nation's third, fourth, and fifth largest beef processors into a single entity.
sentences.zh: 因为它们本质上会将全美第三、第四和第五大牛肉加工商合并为一个实体。

sentences.en: And by the end, just four packers, Tyson, Cargill, JBS, and National Beef Packing, control 85% of the beef industry.
sentences.zh: 最终，只有四家加工商——泰森、嘉吉、JBS和全国牛肉包装公司——控制了85%的牛肉产业。

sentences.en: Compare that to the 1970s.
sentences.zh: 把它和20世纪70年代对比一下。

sentences.en: The four largest packers then controlled only 25% of the market.
sentences.zh: 当时最大的四家加工商只控制了25%的市场份额。

sentences.en: Things are now even more concentrated than they were before the Packers and Stockyards Act of 1921.
sentences.zh: 如今的集中度甚至比1921年《包装商和牧场法案》出台之前还要高。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And we remember before, the impact of all that original consolidation was that these big companies engaged in cost-cutting and in abusive labor practices, which of course led to
sentences.zh: 我们还记得，当初那一波大整合带来的影响是，这些大公司采取了削减成本和虐待劳工的做法，这当然导致了

sentences.en: these horrific warehouse conditions.
sentences.zh: 这些骇人听闻的仓库条件。

sentences.en: What's the impact of all that consolidation this time?
sentences.zh: 这一次所有这些整合带来的影响又是什么？

sentences.en: Well, in some ways, the impact is even more profound because at the same time this is playing out, we're experiencing globalization.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在某些方面，这种影响甚至更为深远，因为在这幕上演的同时，我们正经历着全球化。

sentences.en: I mean, you can now ship goods much more cheaply around the world than you could previously.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，现在向世界各地运送货物的成本比以前便宜得多。

sentences.en: And this becomes a serious source of change in the American economy.
sentences.zh: 这成为了美国经济发生深刻变革的一个根源。

sentences.en: Look, we want to have a fair and open shot at the Chinese market.
sentences.zh: 听着，我们希望公平、公开地进入中国市场。

sentences.en: China enters the world stage.
sentences.zh: 中国登上了世界舞台。

sentences.en: Built on open markets with fair and effective rules.
sentences.zh: 建立在具有公平有效规则的开放市场之上。

sentences.en: Becomes a global trading power.
sentences.zh: 成为了一个全球贸易强国。

sentences.en: I don't believe that our goal should be to close the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我不认为我们的目标应该是关闭美国市场。

sentences.en: market.
sentences.zh: 市场。

sentences.en: I believe our goal should be to make sure that we open up China's market.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们的目标应该是确保我们打开中国市场。

sentences.en: Now, factories, whether they're union or not, discover that they're vulnerable to production being shipped over to China.
sentences.zh: 现在，工厂无论是否有工会，都发现自己面临着生产转移到中国的风险。

sentences.en: Technological transfers, technological sales.
sentences.zh: 技术转让，技术销售。

sentences.en: Where people can make things much more cheaply.
sentences.zh: 人们可以在那里以低得多的成本制造东西。

sentences.en: Where you don't have the same workplace standards.
sentences.zh: 那里的工作场所标准没有那么严格。

sentences.en: Where you don't have environmental restrictions or unions.
sentences.zh: 这里既没有环保限制，也没有工会。

sentences.en: Our administration has concluded more than 200 separate trade agreements.
sentences.zh: 我们政府已经缔结了200多项独立的贸易协定。

sentences.en: Each of which opens someone else's markets wider to American business.
sentences.zh: 其中每一项都为美国企业进一步打开了别人的市场。

sentences.en: And Clinton, of course, is being lobbied by industrial interests who are keen to cut costs so they can reward their shareholders.
sentences.zh: 当然，克林顿正在受到一些工业利益集团的游说，他们急于削减成本以便回报股东。

sentences.en: We fought for NAFTA, which created a free market with our neighbors.
sentences.zh: 我们为北美自由贸易协定而战，它与邻国创造了一个自由市场。

sentences.en: Signs NAFTA, which puts the U.S.
sentences.zh: 签署北美自由贸易协定，将美国置于

sentences.en: in a trade block with Canada and Mexico.
sentences.zh: 与加拿大和墨西哥的贸易集团中。

sentences.en: We have to negotiate trade agreements to open even more markets.
sentences.zh: 我们必须谈判贸易协定，以开拓更多市场。

sentences.en: We will negotiate a conference.
sentences.zh: 我们将协商召开一次会议。

sentences.en: So, for workers in the U.S., there's now a serious vulnerability to seeing their jobs moved elsewhere or their wages downgraded under threat of having production moved elsewhere.
sentences.zh: 因此，对于美国的工人来说，现在面临着严重的不安全感，他们的工作随时可能被转移到别处，或者在生产转移的威胁下工资被降低。

sentences.en: This plant will be here for another hundred years.
sentences.zh: 这家工厂还将在这里再开一百年。

sentences.en: Well, the Janesville, Wisconsin General Motors plant isn't even going to last the rest of the year.
sentences.zh: 然而，威斯康星州简斯维尔的通用汽车工厂甚至撑不到今年年底。

sentences.en: Back in February, Senator Barack Obama made a stop at this plant to make a speech on the economy and to inspire hope in these auto workers.
sentences.zh: 早在2月份，贝拉克·奥巴马参议员就曾造访这家工厂，发表关于经济的演讲，并为这些汽车工人注入希望。

sentences.en: Now, GM has ended that hope by announcing that the company is stopping the production lines.
sentences.zh: 如今，通用汽车宣布关闭生产线，彻底破灭了这份希望。

sentences.en: Large SUVs like the Yukon, Tahoe, and Suburban are all built here.
sentences.zh: 像育空、塔霍和萨博班这样的大型SUV都是在这里制造的。

sentences.en: Around 1,200 jobs are disappearing.
sentences.zh: 大约有1200个工作岗位正在消失。

sentences.en: And a lot of the people who had been able, even with just a high school education, to earn enough in a factory to pay for a middle-class lifestyle,
sentences.zh: 许多原本仅凭高中学历就能在工厂赚够中产阶级生活费的人，

sentences.en: they're now taking jobs at Walmarts.
sentences.zh: 现在却在沃尔玛找了工作。

sentences.en: Celebrated the opening of its 1,000th domestic super center.
sentences.zh: 庆祝其第1000家本土超级中心开业。

sentences.en: Stocking shelves.
sentences.zh: 在货架上补货。

sentences.en: All right, Amazon hiring once again.
sentences.zh: 好吧，亚马逊又在招人了。

sentences.en: The company looking to recruit.
sentences.zh: 该公司正在寻求招聘。

sentences.en: They're working in Amazon warehouses.
sentences.zh: 他们在亚马逊仓库工作。

sentences.en: Workers from fast food chains like McDonald's, Wendy's, KFC.
sentences.zh: 来自麦当劳、温蒂汉堡、肯德基等快餐连锁店的工人。

sentences.en: They're working in low-paid service sector jobs, maybe fast food restaurants.
sentences.zh: 他们在低薪的服务业岗位工作，也许是快餐店。

sentences.en: So a lot of people who've been accustomed to middle-class standards of living are now living on a lot less.
sentences.zh: 因此，许多习惯了中产阶级生活水平的人现在只能靠微薄得多的收入过活。

sentences.en: And they're unhappy about it.
sentences.zh: 他们对此感到很不满。

sentences.en: I'm on the edge of homelessness right now.
sentences.zh: 我现在正处于无家可归的边缘。

sentences.en: Me and my husband, we have to alternate dates.
sentences.zh: 我和我丈夫必须轮流约会。

sentences.en: We eat and we go.
sentences.zh: 我们吃完饭就走。

sentences.en: A lot of people who used to feel a relatively stable economic situation are now suffering constant gnawing insecurity.
sentences.zh: 许多过去觉得经济状况相对稳定的人，现在正经受着持续不断的啃噬内心的不安全感。

sentences.en: Take cattle ranchers.
sentences.zh: 以肉牛牧场主为例。

sentences.en: They used to earn more than 50 cents on the dollar of every dollar that Americans would spend on beef.
sentences.zh: 美国人花在牛肉上的每一美元，他们过去能赚到50多美分。

sentences.en: That number has dropped to a historic low of 37 cents, which explains why, since 1980, we've lost 544,000 beef cattle operations.
sentences.zh: 这个数字已经降到了历史最低的37美分，这解释了为什么自1980年以来，我们已经失去了544,000个肉牛养殖场。

sentences.en: That's beef cattle farms and ranches since 1980.
sentences.zh: 也就是自1980年以来的肉牛农场和牧场。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So that represents 540,000 jobs in our economy that are now just gone.
sentences.zh: 这意味着我们经济中原本存在的54万个工作岗位就这样消失了。

sentences.en: Oh, it's far more jobs.
sentences.zh: 哦，工作岗位远不止这些。

sentences.en: That's just ranches themselves.
sentences.zh: 这仅仅是牧场本身。

sentences.en: So that means, you know, not only are you losing the people within families who are working on those ranches, the maintenance people who take care of irrigation systems,
sentences.zh: 所以这意味着，你知道，你失去的不仅是牧场里工作的家庭成员，还有照顾灌溉系统的维修人员，

sentences.en: the guy who gets hired to drive a tractor, the truck driver who gets enlisted to drive the animals off to the sale barn, all of those jobs are loSt.
sentences.zh: 被雇来开拖拉机的伙计，被请来把动物赶到拍卖场的卡车司机，所有这些工作都失去了。

sentences.en: And at the same time, in the past 25 years, we've lost 75% of the feedlots.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，在过去的25年里，我们失去了75%的饲养场。

sentences.en: That's 83,000 independent feedlots.
sentences.zh: 那是83,000个独立饲养场。

sentences.en: These are the marketing outlets for the cow and calf producers.
sentences.zh: 这些是奶牛和小牛生产者的销售渠道。

sentences.en: You know, the whole competitive infrastructure has just been compressed.
sentences.zh: 你知道，整个竞争基础设施都被压缩了。

sentences.en: And as a result, there are fewer working opportunities for millions of people.
sentences.zh: 结果就是，数百万人的工作机会减少了。

sentences.en: So, Peter, where does all of that leave Steve?
sentences.zh: 那么，彼得，这一切对史蒂夫意味着什么？

sentences.en: Where are we in his story?
sentences.zh: 我们在他的故事里处在什么位置？

sentences.en: Well, this is like the backdrop to the state of things for Steve in recent years.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这就像是近年来史蒂夫所处境况的背景。

sentences.en: And then we get to 2019.
sentences.zh: 然后我们来到了2019年。

sentences.en: It's actually a year that's not looking too bad.
sentences.zh: 这其实是一个看起来还不错的一年。

sentences.en: It's one of the years where Steve thinks he's on track to at least break even.
sentences.zh: 这是史蒂夫认为自己有望至少实现收支平衡的年份之一。

sentences.en: And that year, when he's doing his market calculation, you know, do I sell my calves now?
sentences.zh: 在那一年，当他在做市场计算时，你知道，我是现在卖掉我的小牛吗？

sentences.en: Do I keep feeding them longer and hopefully make more by selling them down the road?
sentences.zh: 我是继续喂养它们更长时间，希望通过以后出售赚更多钱？

sentences.en: He decides that he's feeling bullish.
sentences.zh: 他决定自己看好市场前景。

sentences.en: And he decides he's going to pay to have them placed at a feedlot rather than sell them as calves because he thinks that the market is going to strengthen and he'll get a premium for bigger animals later.
sentences.zh: 他决定花钱把它们送到饲养场，而不是作为小牛卖掉，因为他认为市场会走强，以后卖大动物能拿到溢价。

sentences.en: So, we put them on feed and then everything's looking good.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们把它们送去喂养，然后一切看起来都很好。

sentences.en: The market's going up.
sentences.zh: 市场在上涨。

sentences.en: The futures are going up.
sentences.zh: 期货在上涨。

sentences.en: Beef was selling fine.
sentences.zh: 牛肉卖得很好。

sentences.en: Beef was moving high price.
sentences.zh: 牛肉价格很高。

sentences.en: And then it was when the first rumors of the pandemic, you know, back when it was just in the one city in China.
sentences.zh: 然后大流行的第一批谣言传来了，你知道，当时它还只是中国的一个城市。

sentences.en: Then we start to hear about this coronavirus.
sentences.zh: 然后我们开始听到关于这种冠状病毒的消息。

sentences.en: Investors worldwide start selling everything, including cattle futures.
sentences.zh: 全球投资者开始抛售一切，包括牛期货。

sentences.en: But now, a crash in the market in just the last week.
sentences.zh: 但现在，市场在过去一周内遭遇崩溃。

sentences.en: COVID-19 could cost that industry billions.
sentences.zh: COVID-19可能会让该行业损失数十亿美元。

sentences.en: Cow-calf producers will be hurt the moSt.
sentences.zh: 母牛犊生产者受到的打击最大。

sentences.en: So, Steve thinks this is going to be bad.
sentences.zh: 所以，史蒂夫认为这会很糟糕。

sentences.en: I don't see this getting better anytime soon, so I better find somebody to buy my calves right now.
sentences.zh: 我看不出这能在短期内好转，所以我最好现在就找人买下我的小牛。

sentences.en: He's got three rounds of calves coming up that he needs to sell.
sentences.zh: 他有三批即将出栏的小牛需要出售。

sentences.en: For the first round, he calls up the guy who's feeding his cattle.
sentences.zh: 对于第一批，他打电话给喂养他牛的那个家伙。

sentences.en: Well, this guy has a relationship with JBS, one of the big four meat packers in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这家伙与JBS有合作关系，JBS是美国四大肉类加工商之一。

sentences.en: He called up and said he would not bid on the cattle.
sentences.zh: 他打电话说他不会为这些牛出价。

sentences.en: But if we wanted to get them slaughtered, he could give us a slot.
sentences.zh: 但如果我们想宰杀它们，他可以给我们留个档期。

sentences.en: And if we didn't take that slot, there wasn't any guarantee.
sentences.zh: 如果我们不接受那个档期，那就没有任何保证了。

sentences.en: Basically, what this guy at the feedlot is telling him is, you've got one chance to sell your cows to JBS and get them slaughtered.
sentences.zh: 基本上，饲养场的这家伙告诉他的是，你只有一次机会把你的牛卖给JBS并进行屠宰。

sentences.en: One slot.
sentences.zh: 只有一个档期。

sentences.en: It's got to be on this one specific day.
sentences.zh: 必须是在这一个特定的日子。

sentences.en: It's not up to you.
sentences.zh: 这由不得你。

sentences.en: And you're going to have to take whatever price they decide to give you that day.
sentences.zh: 而且你只能接受他们那天决定给你的任何价格。

sentences.en: And you won't know that price until your animals show up.
sentences.zh: 在你的动物出现之前，你不会知道那个价格。

sentences.en: And I'm thinking, oh, God, I don't want to do that.
sentences.zh: 我在想，天哪，我可不想这么做。

sentences.en: But Steve also sees the writing on the wall with COVID, and he's got to unload his animals right now.
sentences.zh: 但史蒂夫也从新冠疫情中看到了大势所趋，他必须现在就把他的动物脱手。

sentences.en: It's this or nothing.
sentences.zh: 要么这样，要么什么都没有。

sentences.en: And so I go, well, I guess.
sentences.zh: 所以我说，好吧，我猜。

sentences.en: I guess you better take the slot.
sentences.zh: 我想你最好还是接受这个档期吧。

sentences.en: And he's thinking, maybe I'll get $1.30 per head.
sentences.zh: 他在想，也许我能拿到每头1.30美元。

sentences.en: That would be break-even money.
sentences.zh: 那将是保本的钱。

sentences.en: Then he gets a call back from the guy at the feedlot.
sentences.zh: 然后他接到了饲养场那家伙的回电。

sentences.en: Without any consulting or any dealing, they just decided that they were going to pay me $1 a pound.
sentences.zh: 在没有任何商量或交易的情况下，他们直接决定付给我每磅1美元。

sentences.en: They're going to give him $1.
sentences.zh: 他们要给他1美元。

sentences.en: So he's going to lose $0.30 a pound on this round.
sentences.zh: 所以这一轮他每磅要亏损0.30美元。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And he's still got more cattle to sell.
sentences.zh: 而且他还有更多的牛要卖。

sentences.en: So a few weeks pass.
sentences.zh: 于是几周过去了。

sentences.en: Time for the second load.
sentences.zh: 轮到第二批了。

sentences.en: And I said, man, you know, make some phone calls.
sentences.zh: 我说，老兄，你知道的，打几个电话吧。

sentences.en: See if, you know, offer these cattle to somebody else.
sentences.zh: 看看，你知道的，把这些牛提供给别人。

sentences.en: I mean, they're a bargain.
sentences.zh: 我是说，它们很划算。

sentences.en: You know, they're making $500 a head off these cattle.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们从这些牛身上每头能赚500美元。

sentences.en: Surely somebody else will come bid on them.
sentences.zh: 肯定会有其他人来出价的。

sentences.en: But no, nobody else will even come look.
sentences.zh: 但并没有，根本没有人来看一眼。

sentences.en: No one else is even willing to look, let alone make an offer.
sentences.zh: 甚至没有人愿意来看一眼，更不用说出价了。

sentences.en: I mean, this is the spring of 2020.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这是2020年春天。

sentences.en: The slaughterhouses are by then experiencing COVID outbreaks.
sentences.zh: 屠宰场当时正经历着新冠疫情的爆发。

sentences.en: The state of Colorado soon shuts down.
sentences.zh: 科罗拉多州不久后就封城了。

sentences.en: A JBS plant in Greeley, where six people ultimately die.
sentences.zh: 位于格里利的JBS工厂有六人最终死亡。

sentences.en: So there's less capacity at the plants.
sentences.zh: 因此工厂的产能下降了。

sentences.en: And that means there's less demand for cattle.
sentences.zh: 这意味着对牛的需求减少了。

sentences.en: So on the second round, Steve gets $0.90 a pound.
sentences.zh: 所以在第二轮中，史蒂夫每磅拿到0.90美元。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So now he's losing $0.40 a pound.
sentences.zh: 所以现在他每磅要亏损0.40美元。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And what's especially crazy about this is that at that time, consumer demand for beef had never been higher.
sentences.zh: 最疯狂的是，当时消费者对牛肉的需求从未如此高涨。

sentences.en: People were making runs on grocery stores.
sentences.zh: 人们在杂货店疯狂抢购。

sentences.en: They're trying to stock up.
sentences.zh: 他们试图囤货。

sentences.en: They're filling their freezers with provisions for the apocalypse.
sentences.zh: 他们把冰柜塞满，以备末日之需。

sentences.en: They want beef.
sentences.zh: 他们想要牛肉。

sentences.en: And Steve has all these cows.
sentences.zh: 而史蒂夫有这么多的牛。

sentences.en: But with the Packers dominating the middle, there's no way to bridge the two or for Steve to see any gains from this tremendous surge in demand for beef.
sentences.zh: 但由于中间商把持着加工环节，根本无法将两者连接起来，史蒂夫也无法从这股巨大的牛肉需求激增中获得任何收益。

sentences.en: It's all losses.
sentences.zh: 全都是亏损。

sentences.en: Supply and demand, in other words, are totally disconnected.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，供求关系完全脱节了。

sentences.en: Well, they're connected.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它们是连在一起的。

sentences.en: But the Packers are capturing everything that's in the middle.
sentences.zh: 但中间商把中间的所有利润都吞掉了。

sentences.en: So Steve's daughter, Annika, is watching this bizarre moment unfold.
sentences.zh: 所以史蒂夫的女儿安妮卡正看着这个诡异的时刻上演。

sentences.en: Grocery store shelves were empty.
sentences.zh: 杂货店的货架空空如也。

sentences.en: Like, people couldn't find ground beef.
sentences.zh: 就像人们买不到碎牛肉一样。

sentences.en: You could see a cow across the road, and people weren't finding ground beef in Billings, Montana.
sentences.zh: 你明明能看到路对面就有一头牛，但在蒙大拿州比灵斯，人们却买不到碎牛肉。

sentences.en: And she's thinking, this doesn't make any sense.
sentences.zh: 她在想，这根本说不通。

sentences.en: We have more cows than people.
sentences.zh: 我们的牛比人还多。

sentences.en: We have more cows than people.
sentences.zh: 我们的牛比人还多。

sentences.en: At this point, the charters have only this third load of cattle left.
sentences.zh: 此时，养殖户只剩下这第三批牛了。

sentences.en: Forty head.
sentences.zh: 四十头。

sentences.en: And Annika thinks to herself, why would we go back to JBS again?
sentences.zh: 安妮卡心里想，我们为什么还要再去找JBS？

sentences.en: I mean, we know they're just going to stick us with another loss.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我们知道他们只会让我们再吃一次亏。

sentences.en: So she thinks, let's try something different.
sentences.zh: 所以她想，让我们尝试点不同的。

sentences.en: Let's try cutting out the middleman, just like her mother tried to do back in the 1990s.
sentences.zh: 让我们尝试绕过中间商，就像她母亲在20世纪90年代尝试做的那样。

sentences.en: With the grocery store parking lot scheme.
sentences.zh: 用杂货店停车场计划。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It was very nerve-wracking.
sentences.zh: 这让人非常伤脑筋。

sentences.en: We were sticking our neck out here.
sentences.zh: 我们当时是在冒着风险。

sentences.en: We had no idea whether we could sell all those cattle.
sentences.zh: 我们完全不知道能不能把所有的牛都卖掉。

sentences.en: And then, can you get them slaughtered?
sentences.zh: 然后，你能把它们宰杀了吗？

sentences.en: Then you've got all this beef.
sentences.zh: 接着你有了这么多的牛肉。

sentences.en: Well, then you've got to put it somewhere.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那你得把它放到某个地方。

sentences.en: They locate a local slaughterhouse.
sentences.zh: 他们找到了一家当地的屠宰场。

sentences.en: It's pretty small scale, but it's able to slaughter the leftover Forty head.
sentences.zh: 规模相当小，但能够宰杀剩下的四十头牛。

sentences.en: They find cold storage.
sentences.zh: 他们找到了冷库。

sentences.en: Annika has some social media experience, and she makes a Facebook page.
sentences.zh: 安妮卡有一些社交媒体经验，她制作了一个Facebook主页。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: And I posted it, and then it got shared probably, like, I think 10,000 times.
sentences.zh: 我把它发到了网上，然后大概被转发了，我想有1万次吧。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And just around this community.
sentences.zh: 而且就在这个社区周围。

sentences.en: And then...
sentences.zh: 然后……

sentences.en: And they actually do really well.
sentences.zh: 而且他们其实做得很好。

sentences.en: They sell the rest of the Forty cattle, and they make an extra $40,000.
sentences.zh: 他们卖掉了剩下的40头牛，多赚了4万美元。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: With that extra $40,000, I would say, wouldn't you say we probably broke even?
sentences.zh: 有了这多出来的4万美元，我想，你不觉得我们差不多算是收支相抵了吗？

sentences.en: Or maybe...
sentences.zh: 或者说……

sentences.en: From when they were calves?
sentences.zh: 从它们还是牛犊的时候算起？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: I doubt it.
sentences.zh: 我表示怀疑。

sentences.en: I doubt it.
sentences.zh: 我不太相信。

sentences.en: That, like, I do feel like this is...
sentences.zh: 我觉得这……

sentences.en: The first time customers' eyes were wide open, like, they're not in control of their food supply.
sentences.zh: 是消费者第一次大开眼界，意识到他们无法掌控自己的食物供应。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: There is bigger powers that are in control of their food supply.
sentences.zh: 有更大的势力在控制着他们的食物供应。

sentences.en: And that's a really scary thing when it's all about control.
sentences.zh: 当这一切都关乎控制时，这是一件非常可怕的事情。

sentences.en: I mean, like, who do you want controlling your food?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你到底想让谁来控制你的食物？

sentences.en: Who do you want controlling where your food comes from and the price of that food?
sentences.zh: 你想要谁来控制你的食物来源以及食物的价格？

sentences.en: Do you want it one big corporation?
sentences.zh: 你想让一家大企业来控制吗？

sentences.en: Do you want it one big company?
sentences.zh: 你想让一家大公司来控制吗？

sentences.en: Or do you want it...
sentences.zh: 还是说你想……

sentences.en: Do you want it from people like us who are literally fighting all their lives to try and make it better for us as ranchers, which in turn makes it better for the consumer?
sentences.zh: 你是想从像我们这样的人手里买，我们一生都在战斗，试图为我们这些牧场主争取更好的条件，这反过来也为消费者带来了更好的条件？

sentences.en: It's interesting, Peter.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣，彼得。

sentences.en: I do think there was a moment, this moment really early on in the pandemic, where consumers were thinking like this.
sentences.zh: 我的确觉得有过这样一个时刻，在大流行刚开始的时候，消费者们确实是在这样思考的。

sentences.en: They were asking deeper, probing questions about the supply chain and where their products were coming from, because the level of disruption had been so great.
sentences.zh: 他们对供应链以及产品的来源提出了更深入、更探究的问题，因为供应链中断的程度实在是太大了。

sentences.en: And things felt so vulnerable and so broken.
sentences.zh: 人们感到如此脆弱，一切都仿佛崩溃了。

sentences.en: But ultimately, wasn't that what that was?
sentences.zh: 但归根结底，那不就是那么回事吗？

sentences.en: It was a moment.
sentences.zh: 那只是一个短暂的时刻。

sentences.en: And maybe during that moment, people felt good getting their beef from a local rancher or buying masks from somebody selling them down the street.
sentences.zh: 也许在那段时期里，人们从当地牧场主那里买牛肉，或者从街头某个人那里买口罩，会觉得感觉很好。

sentences.en: But once the supply chain started to catch up to the moment, it feels like most of us went back to normal.
sentences.zh: 但一旦供应链开始追赶上来，我们大多数人似乎又回到了常态。

sentences.en: And that meant wanting cheap stuff and easy access to it.
sentences.zh: 而这就意味着想要便宜的东西，并且能轻而易举地买到。

sentences.en: Well, you know, first of all, the supply chain has really not gone back to normal.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，首先，供应链并没有真正恢复正常。

sentences.en: If we ever reach something we'd call normal, there are huge numbers of shortages.
sentences.zh: 如果我们能达到某种我们称之为正常的状态，那也会存在大量的短缺。

sentences.en: We don't have computer chips, so we can't make enough cars.
sentences.zh: 我们没有电脑芯片，所以我们无法生产足够的汽车。

sentences.en: From lumber to paint to workout clothes, we've seen shortages of products, and we've seen prices go up very dramatically.
sentences.zh: 从木材、油漆到健身服，我们见证了各种产品的短缺，我们也看到价格急剧上涨。

sentences.en: This is why the Federal Reserve is raising interest rates and why the stock market is tanking.
sentences.zh: 这就是美联储加息的原因，也是股市暴跌的原因。

sentences.en: And it's also the case that some parts of the American middle class that have been squeezed and diminished for years have seen a momentary readjustment in the balance of power with the giant companies that dominate the American economy.
sentences.zh: 同时这也是事实：美国中产阶级中有一部分人，多年来一直受到挤压和削弱，他们与主导美国经济的巨型公司之间的力量对比，出现了一种短暂的重新调整。

sentences.en: Truck drivers, I mean, there's a job that's really been downgraded.
sentences.zh: 卡车司机，我是说，这曾经是一个真的很不受重视的职业。

sentences.en: Truck drivers are now getting recruitment bonuses.
sentences.zh: 卡车司机现在开始拿招聘奖金了。

sentences.en: They can jump ship and get big raises.
sentences.zh: 他们可以跳槽并获得大幅加薪。

sentences.en: There seems to be a momentary readjustment in the power balance between labor and big business.
sentences.zh: 劳工和大企业之间的权力平衡似乎出现了短暂的重新调整。

sentences.en: But it's not something that likely sticks.
sentences.zh: 但这种情况不太可能持久。

sentences.en: I mean, yeah, okay, Annika shows that you can do an end run around the Packers for some small smidgen of the marketplace.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，好吧，安妮卡表明，你可以绕过那些肉类加工巨头，在广阔的市场中分得一小杯羹。

sentences.en: There's some consumers who've woken up to the fact that the food supply is being dominated by big businesses.
sentences.zh: 有些消费者已经清醒地认识到，食物供应正被大企业所主宰。

sentences.en: They're more inclined to go buy beef from their local rancher.
sentences.zh: 他们更有倾向去向当地的牧场主购买牛肉。

sentences.en: And maybe that's, you know, useful for the handful of people who can take advantage of that.
sentences.zh: 也许这，你知道的，对于少数能够利用这一点的人来说是有用的。

sentences.en: But the big story,
sentences.zh: 但宏大的故事是——

sentences.en: the story of American capitalism being dominated by a handful of well-connected billionaires who have managed to manipulate the system through a lifting of antitrust enforcement,
sentences.zh: 美国资本主义的故事是由少数关系网密布的亿万富翁所主宰的故事，他们通过取消反垄断执法、通过削弱劳工力量，成功操纵了整个系统——

sentences.en: through a diminishing of labor, that story remains in place.
sentences.zh: 那个故事依然存在。

sentences.en: That's the story of the working class and the middle class being wiped out time and again.
sentences.zh: 那正是工人阶级和中产阶级一次又一次被消灭的故事。

sentences.en: We've been seeing this hollowing out across America for decades.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，我们一直目睹着全美各地的这种掏空现象。

sentences.en: And the pandemic presents an interesting test case.
sentences.zh: 大流行病提供了一个有趣的测试案例。

sentences.en: But the basic balance of power remains.
sentences.zh: 但基本的权力平衡依然如故。

sentences.en: When my dad said, my grandpa saw the writing on the wall, he, even at the time when my grandpa was selling cows, it was apparent and maybe more apparent to him than others.
sentences.zh: 就像我父亲说的，我爷爷早就看清了形势，甚至在我爷爷卖牛的那个时代，这一点就很明显了，也许对他的触动比对别人更深。

sentences.en: That was the strategy.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们的策略。

sentences.en: Eventually, they will get into the position, which I think we are seeing now, where they can give us whatever price they'd like.
sentences.zh: 最终，他们会进入一种位置，我想我们现在正见证着这一点，他们可以随心所欲地给我们开价。

sentences.en: And they have.
sentences.zh: 而他们也确实这么做了。

sentences.en: There's things that don't have monetary value.
sentences.zh: 有些东西是没有金钱价值的。

sentences.en: And so it's kind of the shits that it comes down to at the end of that it's just about money.
sentences.zh: 所以到头来只剩下金钱这档子事，真的挺操蛋的。

sentences.en: But, you know, I, you know, all my life, I've pretty much worked seven days a week, 365 days a year.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，我，你知道，我这辈子基本上都是一周工作七天，一年365天连轴转。

sentences.en: I mean, I get a few days off.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我会休几天假。

sentences.en: And, and I'm not complaining because I was doing exactly what I wanted to do, loving it.
sentences.zh: 而且，而且我并不是在抱怨，因为我做的是自己真正想做的事，我热爱它。

sentences.en: But it's also at this stage in life was, well, maybe there's something else, you know, maybe there's something else I could do.
sentences.zh: 但处于人生的这个阶段，也会想，好吧，也许还有别的事，你知道，也许还有别的事情我可以做。

sentences.en: Maybe there's something else I could see.
sentences.zh: 也许还有别的风景我可以去看。

sentences.en: Do you think they're going to?
sentences.zh: 你觉得他们会吗？

sentences.en: Who knows?
sentences.zh: 谁知道呢？

sentences.en: You know, is it what keeps us in it without money?
sentences.zh: 你知道，是什么让我们在没有金钱回报的情况下坚持下去？

sentences.en: Monetary reasons is that we can't stomach quitting.
sentences.zh: 出于金钱以外的原因，那就是我们无法忍受放弃。

sentences.en: Incredible life you got.
sentences.zh: 你过着令人难以置信的生活。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's really special.
sentences.zh: 是的，真的很特别。

sentences.en: Yeah, I don't, I count my blessings every day.
sentences.zh: 是的，我没有，我每天都在数算着自己的福气。

sentences.en: I do.
sentences.zh: 真的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So.
sentences.zh: 所以。

sentences.en: I hear that.
sentences.zh: 我懂。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 行吧。

sentences.en: Have a good trip.
sentences.zh: 一路顺风。

sentences.en: Thanks, Steve.
sentences.zh: 谢谢，史蒂夫。

sentences.en: Bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.en: In a speech last week, President Biden called the consolidation of American industries like beef,
sentences.zh: 在上一周的一次演讲中，拜登总统将牛肉等美国行业的整合称作——

sentences.en: a threat to the free market economy, and vowed to use his power as president to try to reverse it.
sentences.zh: 对自由市场经济的威胁，并誓言要利用他作为总统的权力来试图扭转这一局面。

sentences.en: Look, in too many industries, a handful of giant companies dominate the market in sectors like meat processing, railroads, shipping, and other areas.
sentences.zh: 听着，在太多的行业中，少数几家巨头主导了市场，比如肉类加工、铁路、航运和其他领域。

sentences.en: This isn't a new issue.
sentences.zh: 这并不是一个新问题。

sentences.en: We end up with an industry like the meat processing industry, where four big companies dominate the markets.
sentences.zh: 我们最终落得这样一个行业，比如肉类加工业，四家大公司主导了市场。

sentences.en: Pay ranchers less for their cattle they grow.
sentences.zh: 他们付给牧场主更少的钱来收购他们养殖的牛。

sentences.en: Charge consumers more for beef, hamburger, meat, whatever they're buying.
sentences.zh: 却向消费者收取更高的价格来购买牛肉、汉堡肉，以及他们购买的任何肉制品。

sentences.en: Prices are up.
sentences.zh: 价格上涨了。

sentences.en: Look, I'm a capitaliSt.
sentences.zh: 听着，我是一个资本主义者。

sentences.en: But capitalism without competition is not capitalism.
sentences.zh: 但没有竞争的资本主义就不是资本主义。

sentences.en: It's exploitation.
sentences.zh: 那是剥削。

sentences.zh: 本期节目的报道部分取材于彼得·古德曼的新书《达沃斯人：亿万富翁是如何吞噬世界的》。

sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: I'm here today to express the nation's gratitude to Justice Stephen Breyer for his remarkable career of public service
sentences.zh: 我今天来到这里，是为了表达国家对史蒂芬·布雷耶大法官致以的谢意，感谢他非凡的公共服务生涯，

sentences.en: and his clear-eyed commitment to making our country's laws work for its people.
sentences.zh: 以及他那清晰坚定的承诺：让我国的法律切实为人民服务。

sentences.en: In a speech on Thursday from the White House, President Biden formally accepted the resignation of Supreme Court Justice Stephen Breyer,
sentences.zh: 在周四于白宫发表的一场演讲中，拜登总统正式接受了最高法院大法官史蒂芬·布雷耶的辞职，

sentences.en: whom he praised as a man of principle and civility.
sentences.zh: 并赞誉他是一位讲原则、有礼貌的人。

sentences.en: But let me say a few words about a critically important work of selecting his successor.
sentences.zh: 但请允许我讲几句关于挑选他继任者的至关重要工作。

sentences.en: Turning to Breyer's successor, Biden said he would make his choice by the end of February.
sentences.zh: 在谈到布雷耶的继任者时，拜登表示他将在2月底前做出选择。

sentences.en: And that person will be the first Black woman ever nominated to the United States Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 而这个人将是美国最高法院历史上被提名的第一位黑人女性。

sentences.en: And reaffirmed that it would be a Black woman, saying such an appointment was long overdue.
sentences.zh: 并且重申那将是一位黑人女性，并称这样的任命早已迟来。

sentences.en: I made that commitment during the campaign for president, and I will keep that commitment.
sentences.zh: 我在竞选总统期间做出了这一承诺，我会兑现这个承诺。

sentences.zh: 我不是指他们会不会为了睡觉而喝断片。

sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们睡觉时需要什么样的光线条件，因为这是一个非常具体的问题。
